name: Alaska
climate: Subarctic — extreme cold winters, mild brief summers
transitInfo: People Mover bus in Anchorage — pay cash or buy a Connect Card at transit centers. MACS Transit in Fairbanks. Juneau and most of rural Alaska have no road connections; a car or small plane is essential.

name: Alabama
climate: Subtropical — hot summers, mild winters
transitInfo: No major transit system. Birmingham MAX bus exists but is very limited. Rideshare (Uber/Lyft) is the practical option; a car is strongly recommended.

name: Arizona
climate: Desert — very hot summers, mild winters
transitInfo: Valley Metro light rail and bus in Phoenix/Tempe — use the Valley Metro app or buy day passes at station kiosks. Sun Tran bus in Tucson. Outside these cities a car is required.

name: Arkansas
climate: Humid subtropical — hot summers, cold winters
transitInfo: Rock Region Metro bus in Little Rock offers limited routes. No rail service. Rideshare apps are the main option; a car is essential outside campus.

name: California
climate: Mediterranean to semi-arid — warm dry summers, mild winters
transitInfo: LA Metro (bus + rail) uses a TAP card — buy one at any station for $2 + load value. SF Muni and BART use a Clipper card (tap on/off). San Diego MTS uses Pronto card. Download the respective city app for real-time routes.

name: Colorado
climate: Semi-arid — sunny, cold winters with significant snow
transitInfo: RTD bus and light rail in Denver — load a MyRide card at station vending machines or pay via the RTD Mobile app. Boulder's HOP/SKIP/JUMP buses are free for students. Outside Denver, a car is needed.

name: Connecticut
climate: Humid continental — cold winters, warm humid summers
transitInfo: CT Transit buses run throughout the state — buy multi-ride tickets at transit offices or use the CT Transit app. Metro-North commuter rail connects New Haven and Stamford directly to NYC Grand Central (45–90 min).

name: Delaware
climate: Humid subtropical — moderate, four distinct seasons
transitInfo: DART First State bus covers Wilmington and Newark — pay cash onboard or use a DART card. Amtrak runs frequently through Wilmington station to Philadelphia (30 min) and NYC (1.5 hrs).

name: Washington D.C.
climate: Humid subtropical — hot summers, cold winters
transitInfo: WMATA Metro (subway, 6 lines) + Metrobus — get a SmarTrip card ($2) at any Metro station kiosk and load value onto it; tap in and out at turnstiles. Use the Transit or DC Metro apps for real-time arrivals.

name: Florida
climate: Tropical — hot, humid, hurricane season June–November
transitInfo: Miami-Dade Metrorail + Metrobus use an EASY Card (buy at Metrorail stations). SunRail commuter rail in Orlando. Most Florida cities are car-dependent; rideshare is widely available.

name: Georgia
climate: Humid subtropical — hot summers, mild winters
transitInfo: MARTA subway (2 lines) and bus in Atlanta — use a Breeze card (buy at any MARTA station, $2 + load value). Athens Transit and Savannah Dot buses cover those cities. Outside Atlanta, a car is needed.

name: Hawaii
climate: Tropical — warm year-round, trade winds, occasional heavy rain
transitInfo: TheBus on Oahu is the main option — use a HOLO card (buy at ABC stores or 7-Eleven) or pay cash. Maui Bus and Big Island Transit run but are infrequent. Rideshare available on all major islands.

name: Idaho
climate: Semi-arid — cold winters, warm summers
transitInfo: Valley Ride bus in Boise/Nampa — pay cash or buy passes at the Valley Ride office. No commuter rail. A car is essential in all Idaho cities.

name: Illinois
climate: Humid continental — very cold winters, hot humid summers
transitInfo: Chicago CTA L train (8 lines) and buses use a Ventra card — buy one at any L station ($5 deposit, reloadable via app or kiosk). Metra commuter rail connects suburbs. Use the Transit or Ventra app for real-time tracking.

name: Indiana
climate: Humid continental — cold winters, warm summers
transitInfo: IndyGo bus in Indianapolis — board and pay cash or use the Open Access fareboxes. Bloomington Transit and Purdue CityBus serve campus areas. A car is needed for most travel.

name: Iowa
climate: Humid continental — very cold winters, hot summers
transitInfo: Iowa City Cambus is free for university students. DART bus in Des Moines and CyRide in Ames. Routes are infrequent; use Google Maps for schedules. A car is strongly recommended.

name: Kansas
climate: Humid continental — hot summers, cold winters, tornado risk
transitInfo: Wichita Transit and Topeka Metro offer very limited bus routes. Lawrence Transit serves KU campus. No rail. A car is essential; rideshare coverage is limited outside major cities.

name: Kentucky
climate: Humid subtropical — four distinct seasons, hot summers
transitInfo: TARC bus in Louisville and Lextran in Lexington cover main routes — pay cash onboard or buy passes at transit centers. No commuter rail. A car is recommended for most destinations.

name: Louisiana
climate: Subtropical — hot, humid, hurricane season June–November
transitInfo: New Orleans RTA Streetcar and bus — buy a Jazzy Pass (1-day or monthly) at Walgreens or online. The iconic St. Charles streetcar is a flat fare. Baton Rouge has BR Transit bus. Rideshare is widely used.

name: Maine
climate: Humid continental — very cold snowy winters, mild summers
transitInfo: Metro bus in Portland and The Connector in Bangor/Orono — pay cash or buy passes at transit offices. Amtrak Downeaster runs Portland–Boston (2 hrs). A car is essential outside Portland.

name: Maryland
climate: Humid subtropical — hot summers, cold winters
transitInfo: MTA Baltimore bus and subway use a CharmCard — buy at transit stores or online. MARC commuter rail links Baltimore and suburbs to DC ($7–$9 one-way). DC Metro (WMATA) is accessible from Bethesda and Silver Spring with a SmarTrip card.

name: Massachusetts
climate: Humid continental — cold winters, warm humid summers
transitInfo: MBTA subway (the T, 5 lines), bus, and commuter rail — get a CharlieCard (free at T stations) and load value via the mTicket app or station kiosks. Use the MBTA app for real-time arrivals. Commuter rail extends to Providence, Worcester, and Lowell.

name: Michigan
climate: Humid continental — very cold snowy winters, warm summers
transitInfo: DDOT and SMART buses serve Detroit metro — pay cash or use a Fareset card. TheRide (AATA) in Ann Arbor and CATA in East Lansing serve campus areas well. Detroit has a free Downtown People Mover loop. A car is needed beyond these areas.

name: Minnesota
climate: Humid continental — extremely cold winters, warm summers
transitInfo: Metro Transit light rail (Green + Blue lines) and bus in Minneapolis–St. Paul — use a Go-To card (buy at any rail station for $1 + load value) or tap a credit card. Use the Metro Transit app. The METRO A Line BRT is also useful along Snelling Ave.

name: Mississippi
climate: Humid subtropical — very hot summers, mild winters
transitInfo: JATRAN bus in Jackson offers very limited coverage. No rail transit. Rideshare (Uber/Lyft) is available in Jackson and college towns. A car is essential everywhere in Mississippi.

name: Missouri
climate: Humid continental — hot summers, cold winters
transitInfo: MetroLink light rail and MetroBus in St. Louis — buy stored-value tickets at station kiosks. KC Streetcar in Kansas City is free downtown. RideKC bus requires a Ride KC card or cash. A car is needed outside these corridors.

name: Montana
climate: Semi-arid continental — very cold winters, warm summers
transitInfo: Mountain Line bus in Missoula and Streamline in Bozeman offer limited routes — pay cash onboard. No rail service. A car is absolutely essential everywhere in Montana.

name: Nebraska
climate: Humid continental — cold winters, hot summers
transitInfo: StarTran bus in Lincoln and Metro bus in Omaha — buy passes at transit centers or pay cash. No commuter rail. A car is strongly recommended for everything beyond campus.

name: Nevada
climate: Desert — very hot dry summers, mild winters
transitInfo: RTC bus and BRT (the Deuce and ACE rapid routes) in Las Vegas — use the Ride RTC app to buy passes or pay cash. Regional Connect bus in Reno. No rail in Las Vegas; Amtrak serves Reno. Rideshare is widely available on the Strip.

name: New Hampshire
climate: Humid continental — very cold snowy winters, warm summers
transitInfo: COAST bus in Seacoast region, Manchester Transit, and Advance Transit near Dartmouth. Concord Coach Lines intercity bus runs to Boston South Station. Amtrak is accessible from Lowell, MA. A car is essential for most travel.

name: New Jersey
climate: Humid subtropical/continental — four seasons
transitInfo: NJ Transit bus and rail — buy tickets via the MyTix app or at station vending machines. Direct trains to NYC Penn Station from most NJ cities (30–60 min). PATH train connects Newark/Hoboken to NYC (24/7). Use the NJ Transit app for real-time schedules.

name: New Mexico
climate: Semi-arid — dry, sunny, cold at elevation in winter
transitInfo: ABQ Ride bus in Albuquerque and Rail Runner commuter train (Belen to Santa Fe, ~$2–$9) — use Google Maps for ABQ Ride routes; buy Rail Runner tickets at station kiosks. A car is needed outside Albuquerque.

name: New York
climate: Humid continental — cold winters, hot summers (NYC milder)
transitInfo: NYC Subway (24/7, 472 stations) and MTA bus — tap your bank card directly at turnstiles (OMNY) or use a MetroCard ($1 + load value at kiosks). Upstate: CDTA in Albany, RTS in Rochester. Use the MTA app or Google Maps for routes.

name: North Carolina
climate: Humid subtropical — hot summers, mild winters
transitInfo: GoTriangle bus and Durham Area Transit in Research Triangle — use the GoPass app or pay cash. CATS light rail (Blue Line) in Charlotte with a light rail card. A car is recommended for most travel outside downtown corridors.

name: North Dakota
climate: Humid continental — extremely cold winters, warm summers
transitInfo: Matbus in Fargo and Cities Area Transit in Bismarck — pay cash or buy passes at city offices. No rail transit. A car is absolutely essential in North Dakota.

name: Ohio
climate: Humid continental — cold winters, warm humid summers
transitInfo: COTA bus in Columbus, RTA bus + HealthLine BRT in Cleveland, and Metro bus in Cincinnati — pay cash or buy stored-value passes at transit centers. No subway; use Google Maps for route planning. A car is recommended outside downtown.

name: Oklahoma
climate: Humid subtropical — hot summers, cold winters, tornado risk
transitInfo: EMBARK bus in Oklahoma City and Tulsa Transit — pay cash or buy passes at transit offices. No rail. A car is essential everywhere; rideshare is available in OKC and Tulsa.

name: Oregon
climate: Oceanic — mild rainy winters, warm dry summers
transitInfo: TriMet bus and MAX light rail (6 lines) in Portland — get a Hop Fastpass card (buy at Fred Meyer or online) or tap a contactless card. Lane Transit District in Eugene. Use the TriMet app. Portland is very walkable and bike-friendly.

name: Pennsylvania
climate: Humid continental — cold winters, hot humid summers
transitInfo: SEPTA in Philadelphia — buy a SEPTA Key card at any station ($4.95 + load value) or pay cash on buses. Port Authority (PAT) bus and light rail (T) in Pittsburgh — use a ConnectCard. Amtrak connects Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, and Harrisburg.

name: Rhode Island
climate: Humid continental — cold winters, warm summers
transitInfo: RIPTA bus statewide — pay cash onboard or use a Wave card (buy at RIPTA HQ or Providence City Hall). MBTA commuter rail connects Providence to Boston South Station in ~45 min.

name: South Carolina
climate: Humid subtropical — hot summers, mild winters
transitInfo: COMET bus in Columbia and CARTA bus in Charleston — pay cash or buy passes at transit offices. No commuter rail. A car is needed for most travel; rideshare is available in major cities.

name: South Dakota
climate: Humid continental — cold winters, hot summers
transitInfo: Sioux Area Metro (SAM) bus in Sioux Falls — pay cash or buy passes at City Hall. Rapid City Transit in Rapid City. No rail. A car is essential everywhere in South Dakota.

name: Tennessee
climate: Humid subtropical — hot summers, mild winters
transitInfo: WeGo bus and the Music City Star commuter rail in Nashville — buy a WeGo Smart Card at WeGo Central or transit centers. MATA bus and trolleys in Memphis. A car is recommended for most areas beyond downtown.

name: Texas
climate: Varies: hot/humid in Houston to semi-arid in West TX
transitInfo: CapMetro bus + MetroRail in Austin (CapMetro app), DART bus + light rail in Dallas (GoPass app), Houston Metro bus + light rail (Q card), VIA in San Antonio. Buy regional cards at transit centers or via apps. A car is still highly recommended.

name: Utah
climate: Semi-arid — cold winters, hot dry summers
transitInfo: UTA TRAX light rail (4 lines), FrontRunner commuter rail (Ogden to Provo), and bus throughout Salt Lake City — use the UTA GoRide app or buy an electronic fare card at station kiosks. Tap on/off at platform validators.

name: Vermont
climate: Humid continental — very cold snowy winters, mild summers
transitInfo: Green Mountain Transit (GMT) bus in Burlington and Montpelier — pay cash or buy passes at GMT offices. Amtrak Vermonter runs once daily to NYC (~7 hrs). A car is essential outside Burlington.

name: Virginia
climate: Humid subtropical/continental — four distinct seasons
transitInfo: WMATA Metro accessible from Northern VA (use a SmarTrip card). VRE commuter rail runs Fredericksburg/Manassas to DC on weekdays. GRTC bus in Richmond, HRT bus and light rail in Norfolk. Use the WMATA or Transit app.

name: Washington
climate: Oceanic — mild, very rainy winters, warm dry summers
transitInfo: King County Metro bus + Sound Transit Link light rail in Seattle — tap any contactless bank card or get an ORCA card ($5 at station vending machines, reloadable). Use the Sound Transit or One Bus Away app. Sounder commuter rail connects Tacoma and Everett to Seattle.

name: West Virginia
climate: Humid continental — cold winters, warm summers
transitInfo: Mountain Line Transit in Morgantown (free for WVU students with ID) covers campus and downtown. NICE bus in Huntington. No rail transit. A car is essential for everything outside campus areas.

name: Wisconsin
climate: Humid continental — very cold snowy winters, warm summers
transitInfo: Madison Metro Bus and Milwaukee County Transit (MCTS) — get a Hop Card in Madison (buy at Metro Transit office or online) or pay cash. Milwaukee also has a free downtown streetcar (The Hop). Use the Transit app for real-time arrivals.

name: Wyoming
climate: Semi-arid — very cold winters, warm dry summers, high winds
transitInfo: Laramie's JUMP bus and Cheyenne Transit Program offer very limited routes — pay cash onboard. No rail. A car is absolutely essential in Wyoming.
